### Issue Summary

Since #9182 the invite budget is charged before the invite is created, so recipients whose invite fails still use up the organization's daily budget. Before #9182 the single-invite path recorded usage only when an invite was actually created.

`apps/web/modules/organization/settings/teams/actions.ts` on main (e68a469a):

- `inviteUserAction` calls `applyInviteRateLimit(parsedInput.organizationId)` at line 342, before `inviteUser(...)` at line 344.
- `bulkInviteUsersAction` calls `applyInviteRateLimit(organizationId, invitees.length)` at line 442 for the whole batch, before the per-recipient loop. Recipients that then fail — `user_already_member`, `invite_already_exists`, `duplicate_team_ids`, `invalid_team_ids` from `lib/invite-failure.ts` — are only reported back as `success: false` (lines 467 and 470).
- The onboarding invite action does the same (`apps/web/modules/setup/organization/[organizationId]/invite/actions.ts:36`).

Before #9182 (313470bf, `actions.ts:366`):

```ts
if (inviteId) {
  await recordRateLimitUsage(rateLimitConfigs.actions.inviteMember, parsedInput.organizationId);
```

`checkRateLimit` now takes the units with an atomic `INCRBY`, and nothing in `rate-limit.ts` or `helpers.ts` gives them back.

Example on a self-hosted instance with the default `INVITE_RATE_LIMIT_PER_24_HOURS=50`: a bulk invite of 40 addresses where 15 people are already members creates 25 invites, charges 40, and leaves 10 for the rest of the day.

### Expected Behavior

Only recipients that actually got an invite count against the budget, as before #9182 — for example by refunding the failed count after the bulk loop, or by recording usage per created invite while keeping the up-front check that refuses oversized requests.

### Other information (incl. screenshots, Formbricks version, steps to reproduce,...)

The comment on the Lua script ("Refusing before INCRBY prevents an oversized request from consuming the remaining budget") is about oversized requests, not failed invites, and the PR description does not mention failures either, so I don't think charging them was intended. Close this if it is the anti-abuse trade-off you want.

### Your Environment

Formbricks main at e68a469a (the merge of #9182). Read from source; I have not reproduced it on a running instance.

---

To be upfront about where this came from: I found it with a code review tool I am building ([ReviewGate](https://reviewgate.dev)) while running it over real repositories, then compared the code before and after #9182 by hand before writing this up.

items.body:
## Context

Reported publicly (GitHub #9081) from an external OWASP ASVS 5.0 (L1) static review at commit `37b8c69`, flagged by the reporter as configuration clarity with no exploitable impact. Nothing was tested against our environments. Verified against the repo at that same commit — the observation is accurate.

## Problem

`apps/web/next.config.mjs` sets `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true` next to `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` on two route blocks. Per the CORS spec browsers reject the wildcard origin whenever credentials are requested, so the pair cannot take effect as written: the `Allow-Credentials` header is inert. The wildcard itself is intentional (these are public, unauthenticated client endpoints), which is what makes the credentials header read as a leftover.

## Root cause / where to look

* `apps/web/next.config.mjs:222-233` — the `/api/(v1|v2)/client/:path*` block; `Allow-Credentials` at `:224`, `Allow-Origin: *` at `:225`.
* `apps/web/next.config.mjs:235-247` — the `/api/capture/:path*` block; same pair at `:238-239`.

Two findings that settle the reporter's open question ("if some client flow does need credentials, the wildcard has to become validated origin reflection"):

* **No credentialed flow exists on these routes.** Neither first-party client SDK sets `credentials: "include"` — `packages/js-core/src/lib/common/api.ts:15` and `packages/surveys/src/lib/api-client.ts:135` both use the `fetch` default (`same-origin`). `grep -rn "credentials:" packages/js-core/src packages/surveys/src packages/survey-ui/src apps/web/modules` returns nothing.
* **These routes carry no session. **`apps/web/app/api/v1/client/` and `apps/web/app/api/v2/client/` contain no `cookies()`, `getServerSession`, `auth.api.getSession`, or session-cookie read. They are the public survey-display/response endpoints.

So the first of the reporter's two readings applies: `Allow-Credentials` can be dropped. Because no browser can honour the header as currently paired, removing it is a no-op for browser clients, and non-browser clients ignore CORS entirely — this is not a breaking change.

Separately, `/api/capture/:path*` (`:236`) matches **no route that exists**: there is no `apps/web/app/api/capture/` directory, and the only occurrence of the string `api/capture` in the repo is that config line itself. The whole block looks dead, not just its credentials header.

These two blocks are the only `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials` occurrences in the repo.

## Done when

- [ ] `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials` is removed from the `/api/(v1|v2)/client/:path*` block in `apps/web/next.config.mjs`; `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` and the other CORS headers on that block are unchanged.
- [ ] The `/api/capture/:path*` block is either deleted (no such route exists) or kept with a code comment recording why — not left as-is without a decision.
- [ ] A request to a `/api/v1/client/...` endpoint returns `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` and **no **`Access-Control-Allow-Credentials` header.
- [ ] A survey still loads and submits a response end-to-end through the JS SDK from a third-party origin (the flow these headers exist for).
- [ ] Reply on GitHub #9081 with the outcome — the reporter offered a PR and asked to be told either way.

## Not in scope

Origin reflection / an allowlist for these routes. The wildcard is deliberate for public capture endpoints; ASVS `V3.4.2` is knowingly not applied here.

## Verification level

Config change with no logic — manual header check plus the SDK smoke test above. No new E2E spec (`apps/web/next.config.mjs` has no unit-testable surface today and a header assertion would be churn).
items.title: Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true alongside Allow-Origin: * on /api/*/client and /api/capture

### Summary

This is a self-hosted MCP troubleshooting/documentation finding rather than a Formbricks application bug.

While connecting a self-hosted Formbricks MCP server to ChatGPT, I encountered a failure where the public MCP/OAuth infrastructure appeared to be functioning correctly, but ChatGPT could not successfully complete/use the MCP connection.

The Formbricks instance is exposed through Cloudflare. The root cause was Cloudflare's AI/bot traffic protection interfering with the non-browser, server-to-server traffic used by ChatGPT.

### Why this is difficult to diagnose

Normal browser access worked, and enough of the connection process succeeded that the problem initially appeared to be related to MCP/OAuth/Dynamic Client Registration.

This is misleading because an MCP connection involves different traffic patterns:

- interactive browser/user traffic during authorization;
- automated server-to-server traffic from the AI/MCP client for discovery, registration, token-related operations and subsequent MCP calls.

Cloudflare can allow normal browser traffic while independently classifying and enforcing policy against automated AI Agent traffic.

As a result, successfully testing the Formbricks endpoint in a browser does **not** necessarily prove that ChatGPT can reach/use it as an MCP client.

### Cloudflare configuration involved

Cloudflare currently exposes granular AI traffic controls under:

**Security → Settings → Configure AI bot policies**

with three categories:

- Search
- Agent
- Training

Cloudflare describes **Agent** as:

> Bots that pull information from your site to provide responses to user questions.

That category is directly relevant to an AI client such as ChatGPT communicating with an MCP server on behalf of a user.

The configuration that resulted in a working connection was:

**Agent → Allow (do not block)**

For completeness, I also confirmed that:

- legacy **Block AI bots → Do not block (off)**;
- **Bot Fight Mode → Off**.

After allowing AI Agent traffic, ChatGPT was able to connect successfully.

### Important security distinction

I do **not** think the documentation should recommend disabling Cloudflare security generally.

The useful recommendation is specifically to ensure that legitimate **AI Agent** traffic required by the MCP client is permitted.

Cloudflare's distinction between:

- AI Search crawlers;
- AI Agents acting on behalf of users;
- AI Training crawlers;

is important here. A self-hosted administrator may reasonably choose to block Training crawlers while still allowing Agent traffic required for MCP clients.

### Suggested troubleshooting documentation

For self-hosted Formbricks MCP deployments behind Cloudflare, I suggest adding a troubleshooting note along these lines:

> If an AI client such as ChatGPT cannot connect to your self-hosted MCP server even though the endpoint is accessible in a browser, check Cloudflare Security Events and AI bot policies.
>
> Under **Cloudflare → Security → Settings → Configure AI bot policies**, ensure that **Agent** traffic required by your MCP client is permitted.
>
> Browser traffic and server-to-server MCP traffic may be classified differently, so successful browser access or a successful interactive authorization step does not rule out Cloudflare bot protection as the cause.

It may also be worth mentioning these Cloudflare controls as troubleshooting points:

- AI bot policies, especially **Agent**;
- legacy **Block AI bots**;
- Bot Fight Mode / Super Bot Fight Mode;
- Bot Management;
- WAF custom rules;
- Block / Managed Challenge actions;
- Cloudflare Access policies;
- Security Events / Security Analytics.

### Symptom pattern worth documenting

A particularly deceptive pattern is:

1. MCP/OAuth discovery is reachable.
2. Dynamic Client Registration and/or other preliminary requests may work.
3. The interactive browser authorization flow may work.
4. A later server-to-server OAuth or MCP request from the AI client is classified differently by Cloudflare.
5. The MCP client receives an unexpected/blocked/challenged response and reports what appears to be an OAuth, DCR, or MCP failure.

This means successful browser access should not be used as proof that Cloudflare has been eliminated as a possible cause.

### Result

The before/after result in my self-hosted environment was:

**Cloudflare AI/bot protection interfering**
→ enough of the public service was reachable to make the MCP/OAuth setup appear healthy
→ ChatGPT could not successfully establish/use the MCP connection

**Cloudflare AI Agent traffic allowed**
→ same self-hosted Formbricks environment
→ ChatGPT connection succeeds

No Formbricks application-level workaround was required to resolve this particular failure.

### Limitation

I did not preserve the original Cloudflare Security Event from the failed connection, so I cannot reliably state whether Cloudflare's exact enforcement action was Block, Managed Challenge, HTTP 403, or another bot mitigation action. I don't want to speculate about that part.

The confirmed finding is the before/after behavior associated with allowing Cloudflare AI Agent traffic.

I'm submitting this because the failure mode is extremely easy to mistake for an MCP, OAuth, or Dynamic Client Registration implementation problem, and it may save other self-hosted users considerable troubleshooting time.
items.title: Docs: Cloudflare AI Agent protection can block MCP connections on self-hosted instances

### Issue Summary

Duplicating a survey in the same workspace silently resets configured behavior and security settings on the copy. The most consequential is PIN protection: the duplicate has no PIN, so publishing it without noticing the reset produces an unprotected survey.

"Copy to other workspace" shares the same code path and is affected too, but the same-workspace Duplicate case does not involve workspace compatibility, permissions, or entitlement differences that could justify dropping these settings.

The omitted fields are:

    autoComplete, redirectUrl, inlineTriggers, autoClose, delay,
    publishOn, closeOn, isVerifyEmailEnabled,
    isSingleResponsePerEmailEnabled, isBackButtonHidden,
    isAutoProgressingEnabled, isCaptureIpEnabled, pin,
    displayPercentage, showLanguageSwitch, recaptcha, metadata,
    customHeadScripts, customHeadScriptsMode

Seventeen of these are ordinary survey behavior, presentation, or security configuration: response limit, reCAPTCHA, email verification, one-response-per-email, IP capture, back-button and auto-progress behavior, redirect URL, display percentage, language switch, link metadata, custom head scripts, and related distribution behavior.

`publishOn` and `closeOn` are more plausibly intentional lifecycle resets because every copy starts as a draft. However, there is no explicit reset for them; they disappear through the same incomplete `select` as the other fields. Even if those two dates should reset, that does not explain the other 17 omissions.

`copySurveyToOtherWorkspace` builds the copy by spreading everything `getExistingSurvey` selected:

    const { ...restExistingSurvey } = existingSurvey;
    const surveyData: Prisma.SurveyCreateInput = { ...restExistingSurvey, ... }

There is no per-field reset for these settings — the deliberate overrides are the new identity, copied name, `status: "draft"`, and the workspace/creator connects. So the `select` list is effectively an undocumented copy policy, and any survey column missing from it falls back to its database default. The list has drifted from the Survey model: `singleUse` is copied but `pin` is not, though both are link-access settings in the same card; `displayOption`, `recontactDays`, and `displayLimit` are copied while `displayPercentage` is not.

This is the same omission mechanism previously treated as a bug in #6802, where Formbricks added the missing recontact fields to this `select` so they would survive survey copying.

### Expected Behavior

A same-workspace duplicate preserves user-configured survey behavior and security settings. Identity and lifecycle fields that must differ, such as the new `id`, draft `status`, and unique `slug`, are reset explicitly. Cross-workspace copying may apply documented compatibility or entitlement exceptions, but PIN protection, response limits, reCAPTCHA, email verification, redirect behavior, and similar settings should not silently revert through an incomplete query.

### Other information (incl. screenshots, Formbricks version, steps to reproduce,...)

Steps to reproduce:
1. Create a link survey. Under Settings, set a PIN, a response limit, and a redirect URL.
2. Save, then duplicate it from the survey list's ⋯ menu.
3. Open the copy's Settings — the PIN field is empty, the response limit is gone, the redirect URL is gone.

The copy is created as a draft, so nothing is exposed until it is published; the risk is publishing a duplicate believing the PIN carried over.

File: apps/web/modules/survey/list/lib/survey.ts (`getExistingSurvey`)

### Your Environment

Self-hosted Formbricks

### Issue Summary Publishing a survey without editing its plain-text headline rewrites that headline as serialized Lexical HTML. This report is not about the intended semibold appearance of headlines; it is about that compatibility styling being written back as authored rich-text content even though the author made no content or formatting change. A headline stored as `terra` comes back as: ```

terra

``` There appear to be two causes working together: 1. `toolbar-plugin.tsx` registers a Lexical update listener that serializes the editor to HTML and writes it back to the survey on every committed editor update. It does not distinguish an authored content change from programmatic content imports or selection/focus updates. Focusing the editor can therefore rewrite the survey's local value, which publishing then persists. 2. `localized-editor.tsx` intentionally wraps legacy/plain-text headlines in `

…

` so they retain their default emphasized presentation in the rich-text editor. Cause 1 then persists that compatibility wrapper as authored content. The rich-text headline feature's original test plan in [#6685]() distinguishes loading from editing: existing plain-text headlines should display with their existing emphasis, and convert to HTML when edited. In this case no edit is required for the conversion. ### Expected Behavior Opening, focusing, and publishing an otherwise unchanged survey preserves the stored headline value. Conversion to HTML occurs after the user makes a content or formatting edit, consistent with the backwards-compatibility test plan in [#6685](). The resulting HTML may retain the intended semibold emphasis. ### Other information (incl. screenshots, Formbricks version, steps to reproduce,...) Steps to reproduce: 1. Create a survey from a template whose question headline is stored as plain text. 2. Open it in the editor. Do not change anything. 3. Publish. 4. Inspect the stored survey — the question headline is now HTML-wrapped and bold. This affects surveys whose headlines are still stored as plain text. Creating a survey from a template provides a reproducible path to that state. Files: apps/web/modules/ui/components/editor/components/toolbar-plugin.tsx, apps/web/modules/survey/multi-language-surveys/components/localized-editor.tsx ### Your Environment Self-hosted Formbricks ## Investigation notes **Why the template path reproduces this** Templates were never migrated to rich text, and that is intentional rather than a defect: * All 215 `templates.*_headline` values in `apps/web/locales/en-US.json` are plain strings; none contain HTML. * `apps/web/app/api/v3/surveys/templates/lib/template-to-v3.ts` only remaps the i18n shape into a locale map. There is no markdown or HTML conversion anywhere in the survey-from-template create path. * Rich-text headlines (#6685) shipped read-compatibility only. `localized-editor.tsx` wraps plain text in `

…

` at load time, and the renderer tolerates both forms — `packages/survey-ui/src/components/general/label.tsx` sniffs for HTML and falls back to plain text. Plain-text headlines are therefore a supported storage state, and templates should stay plain text. Moving HTML into the template strings would push markup through [Lingo.dev]() into the 14 non-English locale files, risking tag corruption in every one of them. The fix belongs in the editor write-back, not in the templates. **The write-back needs no user interaction** The report describes focusing the editor as the trigger. Mount alone is enough: 1. `firstRender` starts `true` (`element-form-input/index.tsx:308`). 2. The mount effect (`toolbar-plugin.tsx:264`) calls `setFirstRender(false)` and imports `getText()` — the bold-wrapped HTML. 3. The save listener registers at `toolbar-plugin.tsx:282`, after that import, so the initial import does not write back. 4. `firstRender` flipping `true → false` re-triggers the effect at `toolbar-plugin.tsx:244` (deps `[props.updateTemplate, props.firstRender]`, guarded on `!props.firstRender`). It re-imports the same DOM, this time with the listener live: `$generateHtmlFromNodes` → `setText` → `updateElement`. `localSurvey` is dirtied during render, and publishing persists it. No click or focus is required. `suppressUpdates` does not cover this. It is wired only to the subheader remove button (`element-form-input/index.tsx:510`) behind a 100 ms `setTimeout`, not to the import path. **Fix direction** Root cause is a single update listener that cannot distinguish a programmatic content import from an authored edit. Flag the imports: hold an `isImportingRef` in `toolbar-plugin.tsx`, set it around all three `$generateNodesFromDOM` call sites, and have the update listener skip `setText` while it is set. This fixes the whole class of bug rather than headlines alone, and leaves the `

` load-time wrapper in place so existing plain-text headlines keep their emphasis in the editor. Alongside it, drop the redundant re-import at `toolbar-plugin.tsx:244` for the `firstRender` flip — it re-parses DOM the mount effect has just parsed. Out of scope, worth a follow-up decision: once the user does make a real edit, the stored headline gains `fb-editor-text-bold` classes. Whether headline emphasis should be persisted markup or pure CSS is a separate question.

## Summary

`packages/database/migration/20260625104904_canonicalize_language_codes/migration.ts`'s `run()` executes inside the migration runner's `prisma.$transaction(..., { timeout: 30min })` callback. Steps 3 and 4 of the migration use the `prisma` autocommit handle to commit chunked updates for `Response` and `ContactAttribute` (the two highest-volume tables), but this chunked work still runs *inside* the runner's outer transaction. As a result:

- The chunked phases (steps 3–4) still consume the same 30-minute transaction budget as steps 1–2.
- Locks acquired by steps 1–2 (on `Language`, `SurveyLanguage`, and `Survey` content rows) are held until `run()` returns, i.e. until steps 3–4 also finish.

## Discussion / accepted trade-offs

Per discussion on PR #8407 (review thread on `migration.ts` lines 29-32):

- Response ingestion is not stalled by this: there's no `responseCount` column/trigger on `Survey`, and an insert's `KEY SHARE` lock on the `Survey` FK row is compatible with the content updates' `FOR NO KEY UPDATE` locks. What is blocked is survey *editing* during the migration — already true before this PR.
- The timeout failure mode converges: committed chunks from steps 3–4 survive a transaction rollback/timeout, and retries re-walk mostly read-only ranges, so each retry attempt is progressively faster. Worst case is a crash-looping deploy that converges after a few attempts, not a stuck migration.

Given these mitigations, the PR author chose not to gate PR #8407 on this issue, but agreed it should be tracked as a follow-up.

## Required changes

Either:
1. Add an opt-out in the migration runner (`packages/database/src/scripts/migration-runner.ts`) allowing a migration to declare that it should run partially or fully outside the mega-transaction, or
2. Split this migration into two: a bounded-transaction migration for steps 1–2 (catalog + survey content), and a separate autocommit/chunked migration for steps 3–4 (`Response` + `ContactAttribute`).

## Acceptance criteria

- Chunked, high-volume update phases (Response/ContactAttribute canonicalization, and any future similar work) do not run inside the runner's long-lived transaction.
- Locks from earlier bounded-transaction steps are released before chunked autocommit work begins.
- Existing idempotency/retry behavior of the migration is preserved.

## References

- PR: https://github.com/formbricks/formbricks/pull/8407
- Discussion: https://github.com/formbricks/formbricks/pull/8407#discussion_r3511286832

Requested by: @xernobyl
items.title: Migration runner: chunked autocommit phases still run inside the mega-transaction

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

Formbricks currently lets you shuffle *options* within a question (multiple choice, ranking, matrix rows), but there is no way to randomize the *order of the questions* themselves. For research and methodologically sound surveys this is important to control for order/sequence effects, where the position of a question biases responses to later ones.

### Describe the solution you'd like

A setting to randomize the order in which questions are presented to each respondent, similar to the existing "shuffle options" dropdown. Ideally:

- A survey-level (or question-group-level) toggle to randomize question order.
- The ability to **pin/fix** certain questions in place (e.g. welcome screen, intro, demographics, or a final feedback question), while only the questions in between are shuffled.
- Optionally: randomize within defined blocks/groups rather than the whole survey, so logically related questions stay together.
- The randomized order should be stored per response so results remain analyzable.

### Additional context

- Creating multiple survey variants with different question orders and splitting respondents manually — high maintenance, not truly randomized.
- Abusing logic jumps to build branching paths — complex and not real randomization.

Option shuffling already exists (#248, #3156), so the UX pattern and data model for "shuffle" are established; this would extend the same concept from options to questions.

## Issue

Numeric survey prefill parsing currently accepts JSON literals like `true`, `false`, and `null` as numbers.

Examples:

```text
?npsQuestionId=true
?ratingQuestionId=true
?npsQuestionId=null
```

Current behavior:

* `parseNumber("true")` returns `1`
* `parseNumber("false")` returns `0`
* `parseNumber("null")` returns `0`
* NPS/rating validators can then accept those coerced values as valid numeric prefill answers

Expected behavior: numeric prefill values should only accept actual parsed numbers. JSON booleans/null should be rejected and ignored as invalid prefill values.

## Impact

Malformed or incorrectly generated survey links can silently prefill real NPS/rating answers with unintended values instead of being ignored.

## Fix

`parseNumber` now accepts only finite parsed JSON numbers, avoiding `Number(...)` coercion of booleans/null.

## Tests

Added regression coverage for:

* `parseNumber("true")`, `parseNumber("false")`, and `parseNumber("null")`
* `validateNPS("true")` / `validateNPS("null")`
* `validateRating(..., "true")` / `validateRating(..., "null")`

Verified:

```bash
git diff --check
pnpm vitest run apps/web/modules/survey/link/lib/prefill/parsers.test.ts apps/web/modules/survey/link/lib/prefill/validators.test.ts
pnpm --filter @formbricks/web exec eslint modules/survey/link/lib/prefill/parsers.ts modules/survey/link/lib/prefill/parsers.test.ts modules/survey/link/lib/prefill/validators.test.ts
```

Branch: [https://github.com/bharathkumar39293/formbricks/tree/fix/reject-json-literals-prefill-number](<https://github.com/bharathkumar39293/formbricks/tree/fix/reject-json-literals-prefill-number>)

Hey formbricks team,

I've been building Faultmark, an AI scanner that runs a 
multi-model debate to verify bugs before surfacing them. Ran it on this repo 
as a real-world test and found 4 confirmed bugs, 0 disputed. Sharing before 
posting anything publicly.

---

## 🔴 High Severity (1)

**1. doesNotIncludeAllOf logic is inverted**
`apps/web/lib/surveyLogic/utils.ts:445`

The `doesNotIncludeAllOf` operator currently returns true only when NONE of 
the right values are in the left array, which is `doesNotIncludeAnyOf` 
semantics. It should return true when at least one right value is missing 
from the left array (negation of includesAllOf). This means survey logic 
conditions using this operator silently evaluate to the wrong result.

**Fix:** Change `rightValue.every((v) => !leftValue.includes(v))` to 
`!rightValue.every((v) => leftValue.includes(v))`

---

## 🟡 Medium Severity (3)

<details>
<summary>2. loadInitialDisplays error swallowed — displaysError state never set on load failure</summary>

`apps/web/app/(app)/workspaces/[workspaceId]/surveys/[surveyId]/(analysis)/summary/components/SummaryPage.tsx:108`

When `loadInitialDisplays` catches an error, it calls `toast.error()` but 
never calls `setDisplaysError()`. The `displaysError` state stays null, so 
error-aware UI components like `SummaryImpressions` never show a retry 
interface. Users see an empty list and a toast that disappears, with no way 
to retry.

**Fix:** Add `setDisplaysError(error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error))` 
in the catch block alongside the toast call.
</details>

<details>
<summary>3. enabledLanguageIds may contain undefined values, breaking language enable/disable logic</summary>

`apps/web/lib/survey/service.ts`

`enabledLanguageIds` is built with `.map()` using an early return for 
disabled languages, which creates undefined gaps in the array. The 
`deleteMany` condition `enabled: enabledLanguageIds.includes(languageId)` 
then always evaluates to false for disabled languages, making the deletion 
filter semantically wrong. The `enabled` field also should not be part of 
a `deleteMany` where clause on a join table.

**Fix:** Use `.filter(l => l.enabled).map(l => l.language.id)` instead of 
`.map()` with a conditional return, and remove the `enabled` field from the 
`deleteMany` where clause.
</details>

<details>
<summary>4. createSurvey returns stale segment state after connecting a segment</summary>

`apps/web/lib/survey/service.ts:673`

After `prisma.survey.update()` connects the segment, the function returns a 
`TSurvey` built from the pre-connect survey fetch. The returned object has 
`segment: null` because the database row was updated but never re-read. 
Callers will always see the wrong segment state after survey creation.

**Fix:** After the segment connect, re-fetch the survey with 
`prisma.survey.findUnique({ where: { id: survey.id }, select: selectSurvey })` 
and use that for the `transformedSurvey` construction.
</details>

---

just wanted to be useful and get real-world feedback on the tool.

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

When a survey collects a respondent's date of birth via a Date Input question, there is currently no native way to compute the respondent's age (i.e. a date-difference / time-delta from today) and use that computed value as a number variable for conditional branching later in the survey.

For example, a common use case is:
- Ask for date of birth with a Date Input question.
- Calculate the respondent's current age (today's date minus DOB, in years).
- Use that age in conditional logic, e.g. show an "Under 18" path vs. an "Adult" path.
Currently, Formbricks variables support text and number types, and the Calculate action supports arithmetic on variables — but there is no documented date-type variable or date-difference function inside the survey builder. Hidden fields are externally set and cannot be updated mid-survey, so they don't solve this either.

This forces survey designers to use workarounds such as asking for age directly as a number, asking for an age band, or computing age externally and passing it in as a hidden field — all of which degrade the survey experience or require embedding infrastructure.

### Describe the solution you'd like

Add native date arithmetic support to the survey logic engine. Specifically:

1. **Date-difference function**: Introduce a built-in `date_diff(date_question, today, unit)` calculation (or equivalent) that computes the difference between a Date Input answer and today's date, returning a numeric result in a chosen unit (e.g. years, months, days).
2. **Assign result to a number variable**: Allow the result of this date-difference calculation to be stored in an existing number-type variable via the Calculate action, so it can then be used in all existing conditional logic (e.g. `age_variable >= 18`).
3. **Conditional logic directly on date inputs**: Alternatively (or additionally), allow conditions to be written directly against date questions using operators like "is more than X years ago", "is less than X years ago", etc., without requiring an intermediate variable.
This would enable a fully native DOB → age → conditional branching flow inside the survey builder, without any external preprocessing or workarounds.

### Additional context

**Common use case: age gating**
A typical survey flow would be:
1. Date Input question: "What is your date of birth?"
2. (Internally) Calculate: `age = date_diff(dob_question, today, years)`
3. Logic: If `age < 18` → show under-age path; else → show adult path.
**Current workarounds (and their limitations)**:
- Ask for age directly as a number → loses DOB data, relies on manual user input (error-prone).
- Ask for an age band (e.g. "Under 18 / 18–24 / ...") → coarser data, less flexible branching.
- Compute age externally and pass as a hidden field → requires embedding infrastructure, not usable in standalone/shareable surveys.
This feature would be particularly valuable for healthcare, compliance, and research surveys where age verification or age-stratified logic is required.
items.title: Feature Request: Native date arithmetic / age calculation from Date Input for survey logic

The recent PR #7552 clarified request body shapes in the v2 contact API docs, fixing a mismatch between the spec and actual behavior. With three API versions maintained simultaneously (v1, v2, v3), tracking compatibility across all of them gets harder as the project grows.

A CI check could catch spec drift automatically — things like:
- Request body shape changes (like #7552)
- Fields removed between versions
- Type mismatches between spec and implementation
- Required parameters added without updating docs

Here's a lightweight workflow that checks all three specs on every PR:

```yaml
name: API Compatibility
on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - 'docs/api-reference/**'
      - 'docs/api-v2-reference/**'
      - 'docs/api-v3-reference/**'

jobs:
  check-v2:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: delimit-ai/delimit-action@v1
        with:
          spec: docs/api-v2-reference/openapi.yml

  check-v3:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: delimit-ai/delimit-action@v1
        with:
          spec: docs/api-v3-reference/openapi.yml
```

Example of what the PR comment looks like: https://github.com/delimit-ai/delimit-action-demo/pull/2

No config or API keys needed. Advisory mode by default — posts a comment but doesn't block merges.

### Issue Summary

When submitting an anonymous link survey on an unstable connection, a network timeout
can cause the SDK retry logic to create a second [Response](cci:1://file:///c:/Users/bhara/FormBricks/formbricks/packages/surveys/src/lib/response-queue.ts:165:2-220:3) record. This requires a
specific failure window: the server commits successfully, but the client times out
before receiving the response.
Because anonymous link surveys have no uniqueness constraint for submission attempts,
this can result in duplicate downstream side effects (webhooks, integrations, follow-up emails).
## Why Existing Constraints Don't Cover This
| Flow | Protection |
|------|-----------|
| App survey | displayId @unique |
| Single-use link | @@unique([surveyId, singleUseId]) |
| Anonymous link | No uniqueness constraint |
Anonymous surveys are correctly designed to allow multiple intentional submissions.
However, the same submission attempt should not be recorded twice due to
transport-level retries.
## Proposed Fix
Add an optional idempotency key to the [Response](cci:1://file:///c:/Users/bhara/FormBricks/formbricks/packages/surveys/src/lib/response-queue.ts:165:2-220:3) model:
```prisma
submissionId  String?
@@unique([surveyId, submissionId])
Client: Generate a UUID once per survey session (stored in sessionStorage), attach to all POST attempts.

Server: On unique constraint violation, fetch and return the existing response as 200 OK. Because 

createResponse
 and evaluateResponseQuotas run inside a single Prisma transaction, quota logic does not execute on duplicates, and sendToPipeline is never triggered.

This provides exactly-once semantics for a single submission attempt without affecting intentional multi-response behavior.

Backward Compatibility
submissionId is nullable — older SDK clients continue working unchanged
Only new SDK versions receive idempotency protection
No breaking change
Scope
Anonymous link surveys only
No changes to app or single-use flows
No changes to pipeline contracts or webhook payloads
No changes to quota evaluation logic
Does not change the ability for anonymous surveys to accept multiple independent submissions
Happy to implement if this direction looks right. Open to alternative approaches.

### Expected Behavior

_No response_

None

# Public Survey Results Sharing

## Summary

Allow survey owners to generate shareable public links that display survey results (Summary view with drop-off analysis) to anyone with the link, without requiring authentication.


## Background and Context

Formbricks previously had a public sharing feature using a `resultShareKey` column on the Survey model. This was removed in July 2025 (migration `20250723042907`) due to poor implementation and maintenance overhead.

Back then the difficulty was that the contributor who built that didn't plan the interfaces correctly and every change to the analysis and responses page required changing and testing both the analysis page behind auth as well as the public sharing page which essentially was a copy of the page behind auth trying to reuse some components.

With the reimplementation the goal is to come up with a clear interface to make it easy to maintain the analysis behind auth as well as the public results sharing page.

The use visiting the public sharing page essentially has the same rights as a project-user with read-only access.

## Requirements

### Functional Requirements

**Share Link Generation**
- Users can generate a public share link from the Survey Summary page
- Users can set an optional expiration period: 7 days, 30 days, 90 days, or never
- Generated links should be easily copyable to clipboard
- Users can view all existing share links for a survey
- Users can revoke any share link immediately

**Public Share View**
- Public users can access shared results via the link without logging in
- The view displays:
  - Survey name
  - Summary statistics (impressions, starts, completed, drop-offs, time to complete)
  - Drop-off analysis per question
  - Question-by-question result summaries (charts, percentages, sample responses)
- The view is read-only:
  - No filtering capabilities
  - No clickable links to contacts or other authenticated pages
  - No export or edit functionality
- Revoked or expired links should return a 404 page

### Non-Functional Requirements

**Security**
- Share links must use secure, signed tokens
- Rate limiting must be applied to prevent abuse (suggested: 30 requests/minute per IP)
- Revocation must be immediate (no caching of authorization)

**Privacy**
- PII protection is the survey owner's responsibility
- The public view displays the same response data as the authenticated Summary view

**Performance**
- Public share pages should load without requiring user authentication checks
- Reuse existing summary calculation logic

---

## User Stories

1. **As a survey owner**, I want to generate a shareable link to my survey results so I can share insights with stakeholders who don't have Formbricks accounts.

2. **As a survey owner**, I want to set an expiration on share links so I can control how long the results are accessible.

3. **As a survey owner**, I want to revoke a share link immediately if I shared it by mistake or no longer want it accessible.

4. **As a public viewer**, I want to view survey results without creating an account so I can quickly see the insights shared with me.

5. **As a public viewer**, I want to see the drop-off analysis so I understand where respondents abandoned the survey.


## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Share link can be generated from Survey Summary page with optional expiration
- [ ] Share link can be copied to clipboard
- [ ] Public share page displays summary statistics, drop-offs, and question summaries
- [ ] Public share page has no interactive/authenticated features (filtering, contact links)
- [ ] Share links can be listed and revoked from the Summary page
- [ ] Revoked links return 404
- [ ] Expired links return 404
- [ ] Public share route is rate-limited
- [ ] Unit tests cover token generation/verification and share link CRUD
- [ ] E2E tests cover the full share flow (create, view, revoke)

## Feature Request

Need ability to:
- Invert filters ("Not xyz...")
- Use OR logic instead of AND for filters

**Original Feedback:**
> Filter zu invertieren ("Nicht xyz...") und eine OR-Verknüpfung statt AND wäre auch hilfreich

## Current Implementation Analysis

**Location:** `apps/web/app/(app)/environments/[environmentId]/surveys/[surveyId]/components/ResponseFilter.tsx`

**Current Behavior:**
- All filters are combined with AND logic (line 312: `and` separator between filters)
- Filter conditions are hardcoded (e.g., "Includes either", "Includes all")
- No inversion option exists

**Key Code Locations:**
- Filter UI: `apps/web/app/(app)/environments/[environmentId]/surveys/[surveyId]/components/ResponseFilter.tsx:310-315`
- Filter processing: `apps/web/app/lib/surveys/surveys.ts:249-560` (`getFormattedFilters`)
- Database query building: `apps/web/lib/response/utils.ts:148-637` (`buildWhereClause`)

**Current Filter Logic:**
- Filters are stored in `SelectedFilterValue.filter[]` array
- Each filter has `filterType.filterValue` (operator) and `filterType.filterComboBoxValue` (value)
- All filters are combined with AND in `buildWhereClause()` (line 149: `whereClause.push({ AND: ... })`)

## Proposed Solution (Minimal Code Changes)

1. **Add filter connector type** to `FilterValue`:
   - Add `connector?: "AND" | "OR"` field to each filter
   - Add `inverted?: boolean` field to each filter
   - Default to "AND" and `false` for backward compatibility

2. **Update filter UI**:
   - Add toggle/select for "AND/OR" between filters (replace hardcoded "and" text on line 312)
   - Add "Not" checkbox/toggle for each filter condition
   - Update `ResponseFilter.tsx` to handle these new fields

3. **Update filter processing**:
   - Modify `getFormattedFilters()` to respect connector and inverted flags
   - Update `buildWhereClause()` to build OR conditions when connector is "OR"
   - Wrap filter conditions in `NOT: {...}` when inverted is true

**Files to Modify:**
- `apps/web/app/(app)/environments/[environmentId]/components/ResponseFilterContext.tsx` (add fields to types)
- `apps/web/app/(app)/environments/[environmentId]/surveys/[surveyId]/components/ResponseFilter.tsx` (UI changes)
- `apps/web/app/lib/surveys/surveys.ts` (filter processing logic)
- `apps/web/lib/response/utils.ts` (query building - may need significant changes for OR logic)

**Estimated Effort:** Medium-High (3-5 days)
- OR logic requires restructuring the WHERE clause building
- Need to handle nested AND/OR combinations properly
- UI changes are straightforward but need careful UX design

**Priority:** Medium (feature request)

## Scope (widened 2026-09-03)

Originally opened from GitHub issue #6654, which pointed out that `.dockerignore` was written with `.gitignore` semantics (for example `npm-debug.log*` only matches at the top level in Docker; it needs `**/npm-debug.log*`). A configuration scan on 2026-09-03 found the same file has bigger gaps, and that the Dockerfile layering makes every image build slower than it needs to be. Fix all of it in one pass.

Four things in `.dockerignore` and `apps/web/Dockerfile`:

* `.dockerignore` never excludes `.git` (92 MB), `docs/` (19 MB), `charts/`, `.github/`, `apps/storybook` or `apps/web/playwright`. All of it is uploaded as build context and copied into the installer layer on every build.
* It lists `packages/database/migrations` (see [ENG-2410](https://linear.app/formbricks/issue/ENG-2410/gitignore-the-generated-packagesdatabasemigrations-directory) for whether that path is still generated) and re-includes `packages/database/.env`, a file that is no longer tracked. Patterns copied from `.gitignore` need the `**/` prefix to match below the root.
* The Dockerfile runs `COPY . .` before `pnpm install`, so a one-line source edit re-runs the full install. `docker-build-validation.yml` documents that layer caching was measured as useless for exactly this reason ("reorder the Dockerfile so the install layer survives a source change").
* The installer stage installs cmake, g++, gcc, make, python3 and openssl-dev, then runs `pnpm install --ignore-scripts`, so no native module is ever compiled with them.

## Done when

* `.dockerignore` extended with the paths above, `**/` prefixes fixed, stale entries removed.
* Dockerfile copies `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, `patches/` and the package manifests first, runs `pnpm fetch` with a BuildKit cache mount, then copies sources and installs offline.
* apk toolchain verified unused (sharp ships prebuilt linuxmusl binaries) and dropped.
* `docker-build-validation.yml` passes; image size and build time before/after recorded in the PR.
* Follow-up: revisit the registry cache the workflow comment describes, now that the install layer can survive a source change.

---

Surfaced in a configuration scan with Claude Fable 5.1 on 2026-09-03 (main @ 8c3b9ec). Full audit: [https://claude.ai/code/artifact/e052d7a8-49f3-4d7a-8f02-e05be278920b](<https://claude.ai/code/artifact/e052d7a8-49f3-4d7a-8f02-e05be278920b>)

---

## Original report (GitHub #6654)

Hello, and thank you for your work on this repository!

As part of my research, I am analyzing how developers configure .dockerignore in popular repositories.

During my analysis, I noticed that `/.dockerignore` might have been written under the assumption that .dockerignore and .gitignore follow the same pattern semantics, while they actually differ. In particular, the following pattern drew my attention:

[https://github.com/formbricks/formbricks/blob/84294f9df2199236d2ffee0758165c804737369d/.dockerignore#L26](<https://github.com/formbricks/formbricks/blob/84294f9df2199236d2ffee0758165c804737369d/.dockerignore#L26>)

According to Docker's specification, this pattern matches `npm-debug.log*` only in the top-level directory. (To ignore `npm-debug.log*` in any directory, the .dockerignore file needs to list `**/npm-debug.log*`)

See the [.gitignore doc](<https://git-scm.com/docs/gitignore>), the [.dockerignore doc](<https://docs.docker.com/build/concepts/context/#dockerignore-files>), and [a blog post about the differences](<https://zzz.buzz/2018/05/23/differences-of-rules-between-gitignore-and-dockerignore/>).

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

Yes. While Formbricks already supports Partial Submissions, in some use cases (e.g., timed surveys, assessments, or controlled environments) it’s important to enforce a strict time limit or response threshold. Currently, participants can keep interacting with the survey indefinitely unless they manually submit or until the survey end date is reached. This makes it difficult to run time-bound surveys where respondents should not be able to continue once the allotted time (or defined number of answered questions) has passed.

### Describe the solution you'd like

I would like Formbricks surveys to have an option for time-bound or counter-based auto-submission and closure. Specifically:

- 	**Time-bound auto-submit:** _The survey automatically submits and closes once a specified timer (e.g., 2 minutes, 10 minutes) runs out. Any responses entered up to that point are saved, and the participant can no longer continue._

- 	**Counter-based auto-submit:** _The survey automatically submits and closes once the participant has answered a pre-defined number of questions (e.g., 3 out of 5), regardless of whether more questions remain._

This would make surveys behave more like timed assessments or controlled studies, where the system enforces an endpoint without relying on participants to manually submit.

### Additional context

This feature would be useful in scenarios such as:
	•	Timed assessments or quizzes where strict duration is enforced.
	•	Kiosk or event surveys where respondents only have a fixed interaction window.
	•	Research studies where fairness and comparability across participants require everyone to have the same amount of time.
items.title: Add option to auto-submit and close surveys after timer or question limit

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

Experienced a few pain points when setting up webhooks. 

First issue I encountered was not being able to use "Test Endpoint" to get a full example payload to my local instance. I wanted to webhook to be `x.x.x.x:3001/api/surveys` for local testing, and I expected the "Test Endpoint" button to send a full example payload as per the docs, it does not, just `event: testEndpoint`, The input field for the webhook does not allow IP with port as a URL, and requires a 200 response from the endpoint. Leading to the next issue...

So, I pushed my endpoint live so I could at least add the webhook in FormBricks, however because I wrote the full implementation and the event data is incomplete and fake, my API will as it should throw an error. This error also prevents the creation of the webhook. No API endpoint should just accept the test payload and provide a 200 response.

As I had no way test the payload with "Test Endpoint" I had to push it to test, and given the documentation my first implementation assumed there was an array with 1 element. `body.at(0).data` is what my API endpoint is looking at, which doesn't exist at all in the "Test Enpoint" payload.

To resolve this and be able to add the webhook I had to accept the `testEndpoint`.
```
 const body = await request.json()
 if (!body.event) throw new Error('Missing event type')
 if (body.event === 'testEndpoint') return NextResponse.json({ message: 'Success' })
```


### Describe the solution you'd like

A few items that will help UX...
1. URL allows an IP with a port. 
1. Test Endpoint failures do not prevent the creation of a webhook. Especially 500s. Maybe just check it is reachable, even that I dont see the need for validation.
1. The documentation does not show the payload body in an array: https://formbricks.com/docs/xm-and-surveys/core-features/integrations/webhooks#response-finished

### Additional context

_No response_

Hey guys,

### Issue Summary

API - PUT `/api/v2/management/contact-attribute-keys/[contactAttributeKeyId]` 

The update contact attribute key API's input validation seems incomplete, the user can pass an empty `key` value and the contact attribute key is then updated successfully to have the `key` as an empty string.

Example:
`POST /api/v2/management/contact-attribute-keys/[contactAttributeKeyId]`
JSON payload:
```js
{
    "name": "this is email new",
    "description": "Hey this is email new",
    "key": ""
}
```
This returns a 200 status code and also updates the contact attribute key to have an empty string, this should not be allowed and should ideally return a validation error response.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b2033290-b425-40f8-905b-cd6a2e4e84c0)

Furthermore, when passing an already existing `key` in the JSON payload, the api returns a `500 Internal Server Error` response instead of the expected `409 Conflict` response. This should also be handled correctly for the prisma errrors.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/efb49aa4-2213-403b-94e0-6c8fab576e7a)

### Expected Behavior

The api should return the correct status codes with the right response messages, for the first issue with the empty `key` value, the api should return a validation error response from the zod validation layer.
For the other issue with the conflicting contact attribute key, the api should return a `409 Conflict`

### Other information (incl. screenshots, Formbricks version, steps to reproduce,...)

Steps to reproduce:

1. Make a PUT request to `/api/v2/management/contact-attribute-keys/[contactAttributeKeyId]` with the following example payload (make sure the contact attribute key with the `contactAttributeKeyId` already exists):

```js
{
    "name": "this is email new",
    "description": "Hey this is email new",
    "key": ""
}
```
2. Observe the API response, its a 200 status code with the contact attribute key updated to have an empty string as the `key` field.
3. Make the same api call again but this time set the value of the `key` property to be a key that already exists for the environment, like `email` for example.
4. Observer the API response in this case as well, its a `500 Internal Server Error` instead of the expected `409 Conflict`



### Your Environment

None
items.title: Incomplete input validation for PUT `/api/v2/management/contact-attribute-keys/[contactAttributeKeyId]` api

Survey responses can be deleted from the "Responses" section in the survey details page. Currently, there are two ways to delete a response:

1. From the context menu that appears when a response row is selected via the checkbox in the table.

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

Currenlty we use webhooks on the responseFinished event to propagate the response data to other tools (PDF generation, advanced e-mailing, statistics on 3rd party tools, etc.).

If, for some reason, the webhook endpoint is not available at the time of submission; the response is lost to time and unrecoverable in those external workflows. 

### Describe the solution you'd like

It would be nice to have an option to re-run the `responseFinished` webhook event for a given answer [on a given survey]. 

Preferably via the UI, that way users could be independent when it comes to re-sending the data. 

### Additional context

The payload content would be the same, as to be able to use an external webhook identically as when the user submits it "in real time". 

Eventually it could be a new event (e.g. `responseRetriggered` or something), if that's a cleaner approach.

I've checked previous issues and I don't seem to have found anything related to that.
